1.d4 Nf6 2.Nf3 d5 3.e3 e6 4.b3 c5 5.Bb2.strategy: Develops the bishop on the long diagonal, where it backs up d4 and, once the centre opens, points at Black's kingside. White gets an active bishop without having to play c3.

Brings a second piece to bear on d4, the pawn White's whole set-up rests on, and keeps Black's development simple. White has to keep d4 well guarded before pushing on with the central break, and Black's pieces stay free to castle and fight for the centre.
